name: Troubleshooting, debugging and RCA
note: Questions authored by Claude as practice material. Not sourced from your own notes or any official exam. Verify anything you doubt against the docs.

questions.q: What is the first step when a defect is reported?
options: Reproduce it reliably and note exact steps and environment
Ask for a retest next sprint
questions.why: No reliable repro, no reliable diagnosis.

questions.q: Browser shows an error. Where do you look to see whether the API failed?
questions.why: Network shows request, status code and payload.

questions.q: Which is a root cause rather than a symptom?
options: The webhook handler skips records with a null Cms_Id
questions.why: A root cause explains why the symptom occurs.

questions.q: In the 5 Whys technique, you stop when:
options: You reach a cause you can fix or control
You find a person to blame
questions.why: The number five is a guide, not a rule.

questions.q: What does git bisect help with?
options: Finding the commit that introduced a regression
questions.why: It binary-searches history between a good and a bad commit.

questions.q: What is the difference between severity and priority?
options: Severity is impact of the defect; priority is how soon it should be fixed
questions.why: A cosmetic bug on a launch page can be low severity but high priority.

questions.q: Which of these belongs in a good bug report?
options: Steps to reproduce, expected vs actual result, environment
questions.why: It lets someone else reproduce it.

questions.q: An API call returns HTTP 500. What does that usually suggest?
options: An error on the server side
The user is not logged in
questions.why: 4xx points to the client; 5xx to the server.

questions.q: What is a correlation or trace ID useful for?
options: Following one request across services and logs
questions.why: It ties together the logs for the same request.

questions.q: A test fails only intermittently. What is the best first move?
options: Compare passing and failing runs (data, timing, environment, order) before changing code
questions.why: Find the difference, then fix the cause.

questions.q: A bug disappears when you add logging. What does that hint at?
questions.why: Logging changes timing, hiding a race.

questions.q: What is the point of a blameless RCA?
options: To fix process and system causes without blaming individuals
questions.why: People report honestly when blame is removed.
